claims.text: The German Credit dataset does not allow reliable retrieval of applicants' sex due to joint variable encoding mistakes.
Model accuracy and fairness metrics on the Adult dataset are highly sensitive to the arbitrary $50,000 binary income threshold.
The prediction target labels in the COMPAS dataset measure re-arrest rather than actual re-offense.
Dataset utilization in algorithmic fairness research literature follows a long-tail distribution.
Over 100 datasets surveyed in algorithmic fairness research were utilized in only a single scholarly article.

evidence.description: Existing documentation shows that retrieving the sex of loan applicants is not possible because one feature value was used to encode both married/separated/divorced women and single men.
The arbitrary $50,000 threshold for the binary prediction task is high, and model properties such as accuracy and fairness are very sensitive to it.
The prediction labels Y actually encode re-arrest, instead of re-offense, and are thus clearly influenced by spatially differentiated policing practices.
Dataset utilization in surveyed scholarly works follows a long tail distribution, complementing a short head of nine resources used in ten or more articles.
Over 100 datasets are only used once, also because some of these resources are not publicly available.

methodologies.name: Systematic literature survey and data brief creation
methodologies.description: Surveyed over 500 articles on fair ML across seven major conferences and over twenty workshops (2014–2021), generating standardized data briefs for 226 datasets.
conditions: Title keyword screening for equity-based fairness terminology

methodologies.name: Retrospective deep documentation via Datasheets and Dataset Nutrition Labels
methodologies.description: Compiled comprehensive qualitative datasheets and quantitative dataset nutrition labels for the three most frequently cited algorithmic fairness benchmark datasets.
conditions: Applied to the three most heavily cited datasets identified in the survey

limitations.text: The literature survey is restricted to articles published prior to June 2021.
Lightweight data briefs provide a compact overview rather than full multi-page datasheets for all 226 surveyed datasets.
The algorithmic fairness community suffers from collective documentation debt characterized by opacity of single resources and sparsity of distributed information.
Widely used general-purpose fairness benchmark datasets suffer from contrived prediction tasks, severe coding mistakes, data leakage, and outdated demographic categories.

future_work.text: Update the dataset survey to include literature published after June 2021, such as EAAMO conference proceedings.
Release and maintain a searchable web application for querying dataset data briefs.
